NUMERICAL METHODS

Models, objectives
and parameter uncertainty

Explicit model definitions, fitting options and diagnostics.
Conventions and assumptions are described in the user manual.

Weighted least squares

For weighted least squares with supplied standard deviations in y, the objective is

χ2(θ)=∑i[yi−f(xi;θ)σy,i]2

Here θ denotes the free model parameters. X uncertainties and correlations between data points are not included in this objective.

Weighting conventions ↗
Models and constraints
User-defined formulas, polynomial and cubic-spline functions, and Gaussian, Lorentzian, Voigt and pseudo-Voigt profiles with signed integrated area. Fixed values, bounds and expression links within and across curves.
Optimization
SciPy nonlinear least squares, with Levenberg–Marquardt or trust-region reflective selection. Alternative solvers and differential evolution with local refinement are available.
Diagnostics and uncertainty
Residuals, parameter correlations and local Jacobian covariance; profile likelihood, Monte Carlo, residual bootstrap and block bootstrap. Interpretation depends on the model, constraints and noise assumptions.
Peak definitions ↗Fit diagnostics ↗Uncertainty methods ↗
USER-DEFINED MODELS AND EXTENSIONS

Create your own models,
functions and plugins

Specify the mathematics of your fit, build a reusable function library,
or extend CurveMole with your own Python code.

01 / COMPOSITE FIT MODELS

Define how your functions combine

Build a model from built-in and custom components. Assign addition, subtraction, multiplication, division or convolution, and choose the calculation order. Set initial values, fix parameters, apply bounds or link parameters within and across curves.

Example: five pseudo-Voigt components multiplied by a custom filter-transmittance function. The model expression and composition controls are visible in the parameter panel.

Model composition in the manual ↗
02 / CUSTOM FUNCTION LIBRARY

Write your own analytical functions

Enter a formula in x through Tools → Function Builder. CurveMole detects its parameters; you can assign graphical behaviour and optional derived quantities, then add the definition to your personal function library.

offset + amplitude * exp(-x / tau)
* cos(omega * x + phase)

The example detects amplitude, offset, omega, phase and tau. Function definitions are saved as reusable JSON files and embedded in projects; initial values and bounds are edited in the parameter table.

Function Builder and persistence ↗
03 / PYTHON PLUGINS

Develop your own extensions

Create a Python module with a register(api) entry point and a .curvemole-plugin.json manifest. The plugin API supports model functions, importers, exporters, fitting algorithms, transformations, analyses and interactive panels.

Open File → Plugin Manager to scan your plugin folder, inspect its metadata and review it before enabling it. Plugins execute Python code with your account’s permissions.

Example: the repository’s TSV exporter discovered as a local plugin. The manager shows its identifier, API compatibility and declared capability before loading.

Plugin author guide and runnable examples ↗

WORKED EXAMPLES · SYNTHETIC DATA

Weighted nonlinear
least-squares examples

Three reproducible examples of weighted nonlinear least squares.
Data, fitted models and normalized residuals are shown together.

Fits computed with CurveMole. Figures rendered with Matplotlib. These examples use synthetic data and CurveMole’s Python API. The plotting style was created for this website and does not represent the appearance of the CurveMole desktop interface. Error bars represent supplied ±1σ uncertainties in y. Fits minimize Σ[(y − f(x))/σ]² using those uncertainties. The lower panels show normalized residuals; χ²ᵣ is reported with the data count. The application screenshots in the sections above show the actual CurveMole interface.
01 / SUM OF GAUSSIANS

Two Gaussians and a linear term

Two Gaussian components and a linear term fitted simultaneously to data with nonuniform uncertainties. Individual components are displayed with the linear term added.

y(x) = b₀ + b₁x + G₁(x) + G₂(x)

The fit reports strong parameter correlation (|r| ≥ 0.95), illustrating why residuals and parameter covariance should be examined together.

Fit: CurveMole · Plot: Matplotlib
Website styling; not an application screenshot.

Open in CurveMole ↓Data & residuals ↓Fit report ↗
02 / DAMPED COSINE

Exponentially damped cosine

A user-defined function combines amplitude, frequency, phase, exponential damping and an offset. All five parameters are estimated in one weighted fit.

y(x) = c + A exp(−x/τ) cos(ωx + φ)

A general x–y analysis example: the model is entered as a custom formula using the same engine as the desktop interface.

Fit: CurveMole · Plot: Matplotlib
Website styling; not an application screenshot.

Open in CurveMole ↓Data & residuals ↓Fit report ↗
03 / DIFFERENCE OF EXPONENTIALS

Difference of exponentials

A custom formula combines two exponential terms. The amplitude, offset and two exponential coefficients are refined with explicit parameter bounds.

y(x) = c + A [exp(−k₁x) − exp(−k₂x)]

Nonuniform uncertainties enter the fitting objective explicitly. Bounds separate the two exponential coefficients.

Fit: CurveMole · Plot: Matplotlib
Website styling; not an application screenshot.

MULTI-DATASET ANALYSIS

Independent, sequential
and global fitting

Analyze measurements independently, propagate a model across
a series, or estimate shared parameters in a global fit.

01

Independent

Fit each dataset on its own, with multicore support for built-in functions and custom formulas.

02

Sequential

Propagate a prepared model through a series, inspect changes and pause or resume the sequence.

03

Global simultaneous

Concatenate residuals from selected curves in one optimization, with cross-curve parameter links for shared or related quantities.

Stable desktop packages.
Desktop buttons open the official release page. The PDF button downloads the matching user manual.
Installation notes and package verification are available on the release page.

Windows and macOS downloads are unsigned

CurveMole is a nonprofit project. Signing and certification require fees paid by the developer, so these packages are distributed unsigned. You may need to authorize the first launch.

  • Windows: If SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC”, choose More info → Run anyway.
  • macOS: Drag CurveMole from the DMG to Applications and try opening it once. If blocked, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, then confirm Open and authenticate if asked.

Only approve an official download you trust. Check SHA256SUMS.txt on the release page.
